question: Spring AOP can create a proxy either as a JDK dynamic proxy that implements interfaces or as a generated subclass of the target class. Given a finished proxy configuration (target, interfaces, flags), where is the final choice between the two kinds made? Name the method that makes this choice from the configuration, not the code that fills in the configuration beforehand. Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

In Spring MVC on the Servlet stack (not WebFlux), several annotated controller methods can match the same request. Where is the most specific of them chosen (and a tie between the two best rejected as ambiguous), and where is it defined which of two matching request mappings is more specific for the current request? Name the method that selects the winner and the method that compares two complete request mappings. Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

In the bean container, a singleton bean can be requested again while it is still being created, for example through a circular constructor dependency that no early reference can satisfy. Where does the container notice that this singleton is already being created and fail with an error? Name the method that contains this check for singletons. Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

When a Spring Expression Language expression calls a method on an object and the object's class has several methods of that name, where is it decided which Java method is invoked (an exact argument match first, then the closest match, then one that needs argument conversion, failing when several need conversion)? Name the method that makes this choice. Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

With declarative transactions, a transactional method can be configured with rules that say for which exception types the transaction is rolled back and for which it still commits. When such a method throws, where is it decided which configured rule applies to the thrown exception (when several rules match, which one wins) and how a single rule is matched against the exception's class and its superclasses? Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

In Spring WebFlux, when the value returned by an annotated controller method is written as the response body or rendered through a view, where is the response's content type chosen by matching what the client accepts against what the server can produce (including the producible types declared on the mapping)? Name the method that makes this choice. Name only the method(s) that make this decision, not the methods that call them or the code that acts on the result. Consider only the production Java sources (`*/src/main/java`). Write each method as `Type.method` (list overloads once).

If the private method `ClassUtils.findInterfaceMethodIfPossible` in spring-core (`org.springframework.util.ClassUtils`) changed its behaviour, which production Java files hold code that could be affected through calls, up to three levels up? Consider only the production Java sources (`src/main/java` of every module); tests, Kotlin sources, `integration-tests/`, `buildSrc/` and `framework-docs/` do not count. A call counts for a method when it binds to that method at compile time: an unqualified, `this.` or `super.` call inside its class, a call qualified with its class name (or through a static import), or a call on a variable, field or expression whose declared type is the method's class. A call through an interface or superclass method counts for that interface or superclass method only, not for the classes that implement or override it; naming a class in a string, an annotation or a configuration file is not a call. Method references (`Type::method`, `this::method`) count as calls. A call inside a lambda, anonymous class or local class counts for the enclosing named method. All overloads of a method (same name, same class) count as one method. Constructors count as methods named `Type.Type`. Level 1 is every method that calls `ClassUtils.findInterfaceMethodIfPossible`; level 2 is every method that calls a level-1 method. List every file that contains a call to `ClassUtils.findInterfaceMethodIfPossible`, to a level-1 method or to a level-2 method, once, as a path relative to the repository root. A file that only declares one of these methods, without containing such a call, is not listed.

During application context refresh, `PostProcessorRegistrationDelegate` (spring-context) calls `postProcessBeanFactory(ConfigurableListableBeanFactory)` on each registered post-processor through the interface `org.springframework.beans.factory.config.BeanFactoryPostProcessor`. Which framework classes' implementations of that method can run there? A class counts if it declares its own method body for that method, either because it implements the interface (or abstract class) directly or through any chain of superclasses and superinterfaces. A class that only inherits the body from a superclass does not count; abstract declarations do not count. Anonymous classes and lambdas or method references do not count. Default methods declared in interfaces do not count. Methods of the same name that do not implement this interface (for example protected template methods of application context classes) do not count. Consider only the production Java sources of the repository (`*/src/main/java` in every module; not tests, test fixtures, Kotlin files, `framework-docs/` samples or `buildSrc/`). List each class once by its simple name.

A class counts if it declares its own method body for that method, either because it implements the interface (or abstract class) directly or through any chain of superclasses and superinterfaces. An abstract class that declares a body counts. Consider only the production Java sources of the repository (`*/src/main/java` in every module; not tests, test fixtures, Kotlin files, `framework-docs/` samples or `buildSrc/`). List each class once by its simple name.
